Respondents Veerabhadrashetty vs Prashantha on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102302999/
1  JUDGMENT

This is a petition filed u/s.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, claiming for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief as follows:
On 16-2-2022 at about 9.30 p.m. when the petitioner was crossing the road near Kamakshipalya bus stop, Magadi main road, Bangalore, at that time, rider of the two wheeler bearing reg.No.KA-05-EX-5363 came in a rash and negligent manner without observing any traffic rules and dashed to the petitioner, due to impact,
petitioner had sustained grievous injuries to the head and other parts of the body and he took treatment at MVC No.1620/2022 hospital and spent money for treatment.
It is further stated that petitioner was aged 73 years at the time of accident and was hale and healthy and working as coolie and earning Rs.25,000/-p.m.
On account of the accidental injuries, petitioner is suffering from disability and discomforts.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15 lakhs from the respondents.

3. In response of Tribunal process, the respondent No.1 owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 insurance company appeared through their respective counsel and filed their respective written statement.

The respondent No.1 contended that he has purchased the motor cycle bearing No.KA-05-EX-5363 from one Ramakrishna on 27-1-2022 the documents in respect of the purchase of he said vehicle was transferred in the name of 1 st respondent/Prashantha by the concerned authority/RTO but due to the work pressure and personal inconvenience the first respondent was unable to update the said transactions/developments before the second respondent and got mutate his name in the running policy of MVC No.1620/2022 the said vehicle.
Hence the policy of the said vehicle stands in the name of the earlier owner of the said vehicle which was purchased by the first respondent.

1 St respondent is the rider of the motor cycle ad valid DL at the time accident and 1 st respondent is owner of the motor cycle ad valid policy and RC at the time of the accident, vehicle was insured at the time of the accident by the 1st respondent at the time of the alleged accident and the liability of second respondent only.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
4. The respondent No.2 in its written statement contended that this respondent has not issued a policy of insurance to the 1st respondent.

There is negligence on the part of the petitioner himself to cross the road near Kamakshipalya bus stand, by not observing traffic rules and regulations as contemplated under law, since the petitioner himself was negligent in crossing the road.
The rider of the two wheeler was driving slowly, carefully and following all traffic rules and regulations and hence this respondent is not liable in the eyes of law for any compensation.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

From the above said pleadings my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
Veerabhadrashetty vs Prashantha on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102302999/
2 ISSUES 1.

entities.text: Veerabhadrashetty vs Prashantha on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-05-EX-5363 on 16-2-2022 at about 9.30 p.m. near the Kamakshipalya bus stop, Magadi main road, Bengaluru city ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?
6. The petitioner examined himself as P.W1 and examined two witnesses PW2 and PW3 and got marked Exs.P1 to P22 documents.
The respondents have not lead either oral or documentary evidence.

7. Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
8.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative,
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative,
 Issue No.3 : As per final order  MVC No.1620/2022  for the following:-
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1: In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EX-5363, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 18 documents as Ex-P1 to 18 i.e.,FIR, rough sketch, spot mahazar, IMV report, col.133 notice, charge sheet, CC No.2354/22 order-sheet copy, discharge summary, scan report, blood report, outpatient record, emergency case record, medical bills, prescriptions, adhaar card, 3 bills, OPD slip, x-rays, wound certificate.
10. The counsel for the petitioner contended that accident has been taken place due to the sole rash and negligent riding of the rider of the two wheeler bearing No.KA-05-EX-5363.

On the other hand,
counsel for the respondent No.1 and 2 contended that accident has been taken place due to the sole rash and negligence of the petitioner and contended that as petitioner was crossing the road negligently, accident has been taken place.
Further counsel for the respondent No.2 taken the MVC No.1620/2022 contention that offending vehicle is not involved in the accident.

It was argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 that there was one day delay in lodging the complaint and the vehicle number has not been mentioned in the Ex-P11 certificate given by the hospital and even the MLC has not been produced.

In this regard, learned counsel for the respondent cross examined Veerabhadrashetty vs Prashantha on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102302999/
3 PW-1 at length wherein PW-1 stated that the shop keepers near by the accident spot have stated about the number of the vehicle which caused the accident and soon after the accident, he was unconscious and as such he has not given the vehicle number to the doctor.
Further he stated that he was unconscious and he was in the hospital, there was one day delay in filing the complaint.

11. Apart from this, on perusal of the Ex-P1 FIR, the accident had been taken place on 16-2-2022 at 9.31 p.m. and complaint received on 17-2-2022 at 11.30 a.m. and admittedly soon after the accident,
the petitioner was taken to the hospital and admitted in the hospital as per Ex-P11 and as such there may be delay of one day and above said delay is not fatal to the MVC No.1620/2022 case of petitioner.
Apart from this, on perusal of Ex-P11 history of injuries is stated as pedestrian collusion with two wheeler.

Though admittedly MLC has not been produced by the petitioner, but Ex-P11 and Ex-P10 OPD and emergency case record clearly shows that soon after the accident, petitioner was admitted to the hospital, taken treatment.

Further Ex-P8 discharge against medical advice produced by the petitioner shows that the patient was admitted to the hospital on 16-2- 2022 with the alleged history of RTA at around 9.00p.m. near Kamakshipalya bus stop hit by two wheeler while crossing the road and all these documents clearly establishes the involvement of the vehicle and corroborates the contention of the petitioner.
Even Ex-P4 IMV report clearly shows damages to the front side of the bike and even this document is not at all disputed by the respondents.
Even respondent No.1 or respondent No.2 not explained/given the reasons for the damages which clearly shows that involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Even Ex-P5 MV notice u/s 133 given by the IO to the respondent No.1 and the reply given by him clearly shows MVC No.1620/2022 that involvement of the vehicle.

12. Apart from this, though respondent No.2 counsel disputed the involvement of the vehicle but has not adduced any evidence of either rider of the two wheeler or any eye witness to the accident to prove their contention or to disprove the evidence of PW-1.

Apart from this, though respondent No.1 contended that the accident has been taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner, but Ex-P7 ordersheet in Crime No.2354/22 clearly shows that the rider of the motor cycle has admitted and pleaded guilty and paid the fine in respect of the said offence punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC.

The counsel for the respondent No.2 argued that relying on the decision reported in 1997 ACJ 993-Pankajbhai Chandulal Patel Vs Bharat Transport co., and another and argued that judgment of the criminal court at the most, may provide corroboration to the evidence adduced by the claimant,
but can never be the sole decisive factor qua negligent driving as negligence is required to be established by leading necessary evidence.

entities.text: 1997 ACJ 993-Pankajbhai Chandulal Patel Vs Bharat Transport co., and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. In the line of arguments submitted by the counsel for MVC No.1620/2022 the respondent No.2 if the documents placed on record are perused, soon after the accident, complaint has been lodged by the petitioner as per Ex-P2 and the FIR has been lodged as per Ex-P1 even the number of the vehicle has been mentioned by the petitioner in his complaint.

Apart from this, on perusal of Ex-P2 sketch and Ex-P3 spot mahazar, it clearly shows that rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-05-EX-5363 was riding the vehicle from Sumanahalli towards KHB colony and rider of the motor cycle came from the left side towards the right side of the road and hit to the petitioner.

Further it clearly shows that the petitioner was crossing the road from bus stop and petitioner has already crossed the road and when he was at the edge of the road the rider of the motor cycle deviated from his lane and hit Veerabhadrashetty vs Prashantha on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102302999/
4 to the petitioner.

There was sufficient o space on the road for the rider of the bike to move but inspite of that the rider of the bike has taken the deviation and ride his bike towards the extreme left edge of the road and hit to the bike.
Under these facts, it can be held that the accident had been taken place entirely due to the negligence of the rider of the MVC No.1620/2022 bike 14.

The jurisdictional police after thorough and detailed investigation filed the charge sheet as per Ex-P6 by holding that when the petitioner was crossing the road, rider of the motor cycle came in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the petitioner and thereby caused the accident.
It is pertinent to note here that all these documents has not at all been disputed by the respondent No.1 or 2.
Even the respondent counsel has not examined the IO to disprove the charge sheet.
The evidence of the PW-1 coupled with the police documents clearly establishes that the accident has been caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Apart from this Ex-P7 orderhseet in CC No.2354/2022 wherein rider of the motor cycle has pleaded guilty and paid fine also corroborates the fact that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

15. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- MVC No.1620/2022 Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.

entities.text: Parmeshwari -vs- MVC No.1620/2022 Amir Chand & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
16. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EX-5363.
MVC No.1620/2022 17.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

entities.text: MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656

sentences.text: With this observation issue No.1 in is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.

Veerabhadrashetty vs Prashantha on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102302999/
5 18.
ISSUE NO.2:

As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EX-5363.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
19. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 73 years.
The petitioner has produced the Ex-P14-Aadhaar card which reveals petitioner's date of birth is 1949 and as on the date of accident,
petitioner
was aged about 73 years.
The petitioner has stated that he was MVC No.1620/2022 doing coolie work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any document regarding his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of his work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,500/- p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
20. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:-
As per the medical records i.e., Ex-P18-wound certificate the petitioner has sustained injuries i.e.,(1) head injury with EDH, fracture right temporal bone (2) contusion right shoulder.
The doctor has opined that the injuries No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.
Further petitioner has produced Ex-P8 discharge summary of Madhu hospital which reveals petitioner had sustained head injury, right shoulder pain, abrasion wound over right side of frontal region.

Ex-P9-CT scan of brain (plaint) reveals extra dural hematoma MVC No.1620/2022 noted in the right anterior temporal convexity measuring 7 mm thickness, contusion noted in the right temporal region, fracture of right temporal bone involving squamous and mastoid parts with collection in the right middle ear cavity and mastoid air cells.
Age related cerebral and cerebellar degeneration.
Bilateral maxillary and right ethmoidal sinusitis noted.
Fronto temporal pericranial soft tissue swelling noted.

Further petitioner got examined one Raghunath T. -Medical record officer at Madhu hospital,
Bengaluru as PW-3 who has produced Ex-P21 and 22- authorisation letter and case sheet.
21 . It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.
Therefore he got examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW.2 who stated that, petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., right scapular neck fracture with right clavicle fracture and head injury.

PW-2 further stated that petitioner was treated at Sanjay Gandhi hospital conservatively with shoulder immobilizer, petitioner was on regular followup in the same hospital and the fracture untied with right shoulder stiffness.
MVC No.1620/2022 PW-2 assessed the disability of right arm at 28% and wholebody physical disability at 9%.

Veerabhadrashetty vs Prashantha on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102302999/
6 22.
During cross examination of PW-2 admitted that fractured bones are united.
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar -vs- Ajay Kumar and Another.
23.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Nagaraj. B.N as PW.2, who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has total disability of the right arm at MVC No.1620/2022 28% and wholebody physical disability at 9%.
24.
It is relevant to note that right scapular neck fracture with right clavicle fracture and head injury.
It is in this view of the matter, no disability is prescribed for clavicle fracture in the Government of India guidelines 2018.
Despite of it, PW.2 has assessed the whole body disability of the petitioner at 9% which is totally contrary to the guidelines.
Be that as it may as the clavicle fracture does not lead to any disability the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

25. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the fractures and grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and petitioner had sustained injuries i.e., (1)
head injury with EDH, fracture right temporal bone (2) contusion right shoulder.
The doctor has opined that the injuries No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.
The petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Madhu hospital.
The petitioner has stated that he is suffering with MVC No.1620/2022 permanent disablement and deformity to attend his work and to do daily activities.
Hence petitioner is suffering from whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.

On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 73 years,
certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

26. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 3 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.46,500/- (15,500 X 3) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.

Veerabhadrashetty vs Prashantha on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102302999/
7 27.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, MVC No.1620/2022 petitioner is a resident of Gollarahosahalli, Channarayanapatna, Hasan and has taken treatment at Madhu Multi speciality hospital and Sanjay Gandhi hospital Bangalore and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.6,000/- under this head.
28. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under this head.
MVC No.1620/2022 29. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the medical bills as per Ex.P.12 for Rs.20,750/- and medical prescriptions at Ex-P13.
Ex - P15
medical bills for Rs.3116=30.
Out of the said medical bills, one bill i.e., Sl.No.15 reveals the date 12-3-2021 for Rs.800/- i.e., prior to the accident.
Hence, the said bill deducted from the total medical bill.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.23,066/- under the head of medical expenses.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:-

1 Pain & sufferings : Rs. 1,00,000=00 2 Loss of income during : Rs. 46,500=00 laid-up period 3 Attendant charges, extra : Rs. 6,000=00 nutritious food &
conveyance charges 4 Loss of future amenities : Rs. 25,000=00 & happiness

5 Medical expenses : Rs. 23,066=00 MVC No.1620/2022 Total Rs. 2,00,566=00 Hence petitioner is entitle for compensation of Rs.2,00,566=00.
30.
INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

Veerabhadrashetty vs Prashantha on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102302999/
8 31.

Counsel for the respondent No.1 taken the contention that he has purchased the two wheeler bearing reg.No.KA-05- EX-5363 from one Ramesh on 27-1-2022 and documents in respect of the purchase of the said vehicle was transferred in the name of first respondent by the concerned RTO,
but due to the work pressure and personal inconvenience first respondent was unable to update same before 2nd respondent authority and got his name in the policy of the said vehicle and hence the policy of the said vehicle was stands in the name of earlier owner of the said vehicle.
In the mean while accident had been taken place and subsequent to accident, 2 nd respondent MVC No.1620/2022 authority has mutated the name of the first respondent of the same policy number.
32. But there is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy by 2nd respondent and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
33. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
-: O R D E R :-
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of MVC No.1620/2022 Rs.2,00,566/-
with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, entire amount shall be released to him through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 8th day of November 2024).

(Chetana S.F.) IV Addl., Small Cause Judge & ACJM, Court of Small Causes,

The jurisdictional police after thorough and detailed investigation filed the charge sheet as per Ex-P6 by holding that when the petitioner was crossing the road, rider of the motor cycle came in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the petitioner and thereby caused the accident.
The evidence of the PW-1 coupled with the police documents clearly establishes that the accident has been caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Apart from this Ex-P7 orderhseet in CC No.2354/2022 wherein rider of the motor cycle has pleaded guilty and paid fine also corroborates the fact that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
16. Thus, the oral evidence of PW-1 discussed with the above documentary evidence are sufficient for the purpose of the actionable claim under the Motor Vehicles Act.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EX-5363.
MVC No.1620/2022 17.
In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.
MVC No.1620/2022 PW-2 assessed the disability of right arm at 28% and wholebody physical disability at 9%.
From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.
Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and lost his earning capacity.
It is relevant to note that right scapular neck fracture with right clavicle fracture and head injury.
It is in this view of the matter, no disability is prescribed for clavicle fracture in the Government of India guidelines 2018.
Despite of it, PW.2 has assessed the whole body disability of the petitioner at 9% which is totally contrary to the guidelines.
Be that as it may as the clavicle fracture does not lead to any disability the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards Rs.46,500/- (15,500 X 3) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
